**Where we are ahead:** the shape and the hostile-input story. The module reads straight into the collection's typed
`dataframe.Frame` (decimals rescaled to 12 digits, timestamps and durations in microseconds, dictionaries as
categoricals, lists and structs as columns) and writes one back, where the others hand over Arrow's own arrays;
every limit that bounds an allocation is checked before the work it bounds (a 2.5 KB schema naming 2^64 fields, a
zstd bomb across many messages, K footer blocks naming one message), against a reviewer's findings and a
deterministic fuzz driver, with a read that ends in an error and never in a crash; UTF-8 is checked by default
(arrow-rs does too; C++ makes it a separate `Validate` call *(inferred)*); the anchor is the Arrow integration
golden files compared with their JSON through an oracle written from the JSON's own encoding; pure Zig with
ZSTD built in both ways, no C, no `libarrow`. Nothing here is a measured lead, so the scope is not `ahead`.
**Where we are behind** (all in Backlog): the types the format has and `dataframe` has no column for (Union,
Interval) are refused; Map is read as a list of its entries struct, so a write-back loses the "map" tag (Arrow C++,
arrow-rs and polars 2.x keep a map type of their own); the view types, RunEndEncoded, Map and Decimal32/64/256 are
read but never written; LZ4_FRAME, the
other codec every Arrow implementation but this one has and the default of pyarrow's Feather writer, is refused
(waits for an `lz4` module); there is no
zero-copy or memory-mapped read, no incremental reader or writer over `std.Io` (the input and the
output are whole byte slices), no big-endian byte swap; the writer's output has not been read by a foreign
implementation and no speed was measured.

## What this module is, and what it is not

Apache Arrow IPC — the stream format and the file (Feather v2) format — between bytes and a whole
`dataframe.Frame`: `writeStream` / `writeFile` turn a frame into Arrow, `readStream` / `readFile` read one back,
`openFile` gives random access to a file's record batches, ZSTD body compression both ways, the schema's, fields'
and file footer's key/value metadata both ways (`ReadOptions.metadata`, `WriteOptions.schema_metadata` /
`field_metadata` / `footer_metadata`: `dataframe.Frame` has no slot for it), column projection on read
(`ReadOptions.columns`). Underneath, a
bounds-checked FlatBuffers reader and builder, the `Schema.fbs` / `Message.fbs` / `File.fbs` tables, and the
message framing, each usable on its own (`arrow.fb`, `arrow.schema`, `arrow.ipc`). Every input is untrusted: a
hostile stream ends in an error, within the limits below, never in a crash or an unbounded allocation.

**Not here:** the Arrow C data interface (sharing buffers with another library in the same process), Flight
(RPC), compute kernels, a columnar in-memory representation of its own (the reader decodes into `dataframe`'s
storage and copies every buffer — no zero-copy views over the input), Parquet, the JSON integration format as an
output, and the types `dataframe` has no column for (Interval, Union) — those are refused
(`Unsupported`). RunEndEncoded is read expanded into a plain column, BinaryView / Utf8View as `binary` /
`text`, ListView / LargeListView as `list`, Map as a `list` of its entries `struct`, Decimal32 / Decimal64 /
Decimal256 as `decimal`; none of them is written. LZ4_FRAME body compression is refused until the
collection has an LZ4 codec (deferred, not refused for good).

## Wire format / algorithm

Apache Arrow columnar format 1.x, metadata version V5: `Schema.fbs`, `Message.fbs` (FlatBuffers, `src/fb.zig`,
`src/schema.zig`), the encapsulated message framing (continuation marker `0xFFFFFFFF`, metadata length, metadata
padded to 8, body; `src/ipc.zig`) and the stream format: `Schema`, then the `DictionaryBatch`es, then the
`RecordBatch`es, then the end-of-stream marker (`src/stream.zig`). The file format (wave A4) is `ARROW1` and two
zero bytes, the same stream, then a `Footer` table (`File.fbs`: version, schema, a `Block` per dictionary and per
record batch — offset of the message's framing, framing + padded metadata length, body length; 24-byte structs),
its `int32` length and `ARROW1`; `openFile` reads the footer's schema, decodes the dictionaries and checks every
batch's metadata, and `File.readBatch(i)` decodes one batch on demand. Buffers are written 64-byte aligned and padded;
any 8-byte layout is read. Validity bitmaps are LSB-first, a buffer of length 0 when the array has no null.

**Body compression (wave A5).** `Message.fbs` `BodyCompression`, method BUFFER: each buffer of a record or
dictionary batch is compressed on its own and starts with its uncompressed length as a little-endian `int64`; -1
means the bytes after it are stored raw; a buffer of length 0 stays empty. `WriteOptions.compression = .zstd`
(level `compression_level`, 0 = zstd's 3) compresses every non-empty buffer with the collection's `zstd` module and
stores raw the ones that do not shrink, as Arrow C++ and arrow-rs do. The reader decompresses ZSTD (one zstd context
per read) after checking each declared length against `zstd.decompressBound` and the whole read's total against
`ReadOptions.max_body_bytes`; LZ4_FRAME is `error.Unsupported` (the collection has no LZ4 codec).

**Type mapping (wave A2).** The writer maps the column's DECLARED `ColumnType` and reads the cells through
`ColumnData.get`, so storage of another kind that holds values of the declared type is written too:

| `dataframe` | Arrow written | Arrow also read |
|---|---|---|
| `int` / `int8`..`int32` / `uint8`..`uint64` | Int64 / Int8..Int32 / UInt8..UInt64 | — |
| `float` / `float32` | Float64 / Float32 | Float16 → `float32` |
| `bool` | Bool (bit-packed) | — |
| `decimal` (i128, 12 digits) | Decimal128(p, 12), p = digits of the widest value (≥ 12); 39 digits → `Unsupported` | Decimal128(p, s) rescaled to 12 digits; inexact, out of range, wider than p or than 38 digits → `Unsupported`, or null under `lossy`. Decimal32 / Decimal64 widened exactly, then the same; Decimal256 when the value fits an i128, else the same refusal |
| `text` / `binary` | Utf8 (UTF-8 checked) / Binary; Large* from `WriteOptions.large_from` bytes (default 2^31) | LargeUtf8 / LargeBinary; FixedSizeBinary → `binary` |
| `date` (ISO text) | Date32 (days) | Date64 (ms; off a day boundary → `Unsupported`, floored to the containing day under `lossy`); years outside 0000–9999 → `Unsupported` |
| `timestamp` (+ `time_zone`) | Timestamp(us, zone) | s / ms / ns (ns not divisible to us → `Unsupported`, truncated toward zero under `lossy`); a zone `tz` does not know → `Unsupported`, or under `lossy` a naive column (the cells are UTC instants either way) |
| `duration` | Duration(us) | s / ms / ns (ns as for timestamps) |
| `time` | Time64(us) | Time32(s, ms), Time64(ns, as for timestamps); a value outside `[0, 24h)` (Arrow allows 24:00:00) → `Unsupported`, or null under `lossy` |
| `categorical` | Utf8, dictionary-encoded, Int32 indices, `ordered` kept | any integer index type; an unordered dictionary is deduplicated and sorted lexically (the `CatColumn` invariant), an ordered one deduplicated in its order; null dictionary entries read as null rows; a dictionary replaced in a stream: the union of the dictionaries the rows use (see "Dictionaries") |
| `list` (`inner[0]`) | List (Int32 offsets) | LargeList; null rows with elements and offsets not starting at 0 are compacted |
| `array` (`array_width`) | FixedSizeList(width) | — |
| `struct` (`inner`) | Struct | — |
| `.nulls` storage with no declaration (a list's elements) | Null | Null → `text` with no storage (what `readJson` gives an all-null column) |
| `boxed` storage | `Unsupported` (no Arrow type short of a dense union) | — |
| (the values' column) | — | RunEndEncoded (Int16/32/64 run ends) → the values' type, runs expanded |
| `text` / `binary` / `list` | — | Utf8View / BinaryView (inline or variadic-buffer views, copied) / ListView, LargeListView (offsets + sizes, copied) |
| `list` of `struct` (key, value) | — | Map: a list of its entries struct under the file's own field names (`entries` / `key` / `value` when canonical), `keysSorted` dropped; written back as a List of Struct (the "map" tag is lost) |

**Map (2026-11-17, owner decision).** `dataframe` has no map column, so a Map reads as what it physically is,
`list<struct<key, value>>` — what polars read it as until 1.39 (`DataType::List` of the entries field;
polars-core `datatypes/field.rs`) and still does without its `dtype-map` feature, and what pandas gets from
pyarrow (a list of `(key, value)` tuples). Arrow C++ (`MapType`), arrow-rs (`DataType::Map`) and polars 2.x
(`dtype-map`, on in its Python build) keep a map type of their own; a write-back from this module is a List of
Struct. Field names are kept as the file gives them, as arrow-rs does (`ipc/convert.rs`); Arrow C++ renames the
key and value fields to `key` / `value` on read and writes the entries as `entries`. The rules both C++
(`ipc/metadata_internal.cc`, `MapArray::ValidateChildData`) and arrow-rs (`MapArray::try_new`) enforce, as
Schema.fbs states them ("neither the entries field nor the key field may be nullable"), are `error.Malformed`
here: a Map field without exactly one child, entries that are not a struct of two fields (or are
dictionary-encoded), a nullable entries or key field, and a batch whose entries or keys hold a null (a non-zero
null count on either node).

**Run-end encoded metadata (2026-11-17).** `ReadOptions.metadata` reports a RunEndEncoded field in the shape of
the column it reads as: the field's own pairs, and as its children the `values` field's children (through
nested run-end fields); the `run_ends` and `values` fields' own pairs are dropped. Arrow C++'s IPC reader does
the same — it rebuilds the type from the two children's TYPES only (`ipc/metadata_internal.cc`,
`RunEndEncodedType(children[0]->type(), children[1]->type())`), so neither child's name, nullability nor metadata
survives a read there either; the values' own children (a struct's fields) keep theirs as part of the type. So
`WriteOptions.field_metadata` taken from a read always fits the frame: a run-end encoded struct's child metadata
lands on the struct's own fields, never on the `run_ends` / `values` pair.

**Dictionaries (2026-11-17).** A dictionary over a non-text type (Int64 values, say) is read as a plain column of
that type. A dictionary may sit anywhere in the schema: in a list or struct (a `list` / `struct` of `categorical`),
shared by several fields, and inside another dictionary's values (the `nested_dictionary` golden: a dictionary of
lists whose items are dictionary-encoded reads as a `list` of `categorical`) — the inner one is decoded first, as
Arrow C++ resolves it. Deltas (`isDelta`) extend a dictionary; a delta for a dictionary not yet sent is
`error.Malformed` (Arrow C++ `DictionaryMemo::AddDictionaryDelta` and arrow-rs `update_dictionaries` refuse it).

*Replacement.* In a STREAM a non-delta `DictionaryBatch` for an id already seen replaces the dictionary
(Columnar.rst, "IPC Streaming Format"): the record batches read before it keep indexing the old one, those after it
index the new one (and its deltas); each batch's indices are checked against the dictionary current when it was read.
This is what Arrow C++'s `RecordBatchStreamReader` (`DictionaryMemo::AddOrReplaceDictionary`, a
`num_replaced_dictionaries` statistic) and arrow-rs's `StreamReader` (`update_dictionaries` inserts the new values)
do: each record batch carries its own dictionary. A frame is one column, not a chunked array, so the batches merge
the way pyarrow's `read_all().to_pandas()` merges a chunked dictionary column (`arrow_to_pandas.cc`
`NeedDictionaryUnification` / `DictionaryUnifier`): the categories are the union of the dictionaries the rows use,
deduplicated in order of first appearance, `ordered` kept. An ordered column keeps that order; an unordered one is
then sorted lexically like every unordered dictionary this module reads. A dictionary replaced before any batch used
it adds no category; a read with no record batch keeps the first dictionary's. A non-text dictionary needs no
merging: each row reads its value from its own generation. In a FILE replacement is forbidden ("The IPC File format
does not support dictionary replacement, i.e. only one non-delta dictionary batch can be emitted for a given
dictionary ID", Columnar.rst, "Deviations from the IPC Streaming Format"), and Arrow C++'s file reader fails with
`Status::Invalid` ("Unsupported dictionary replacement in IPC file"): `error.Malformed` here (before 2026-11-17 a
replacement was `Unsupported` in both formats). Every generation's entries are kept and charged (see Limits), so N
replacements of a dictionary cost N dictionaries.

Each dictionary-encoded column gets its own id, its whole dictionary written once before the first record batch.

## Limits and refusals

Every limit is checked before the work it bounds; past one the read is `error.LimitExceeded` (an option) or
`error.Malformed` (more than the input could honestly describe). Tests: `src/hostile_test.zig` builds each
hostile shape with `fb.Builder` and reads it under a byte-capped allocator; `src/stream_test.zig`
"targeted corruptions", "every truncation and byte flip".

- **Schema decode budget** (not an option): FlatBuffers offsets may share tables, so a few KB of metadata can
  name 2^64 fields through children vectors pointing at one table. `schema.decodeSchema` charges 16 units per
  `Field` and `KeyValue` and one per byte of every name, zone, metadata key and metadata value string against
  `2 × metadata length + 64`; past it `error.Malformed` (a footer's `custom_metadata` gets the same budget from
  the footer's length). An honest schema spends at most about its length (every field needs more than 8 unique
  bytes plus its name). Nesting deeper than `schema.max_depth` (64) is refused on both sides.
- `ReadOptions.max_rows` (default 2^27, ours): the most rows any one array may claim — the frame's rows summed over
  the batches, a list's elements, a dictionary's entries (every generation of a replaced dictionary together, deltas
  included), a run-end array's runs.
- `ReadOptions.max_cells` (default 2^28, ours): the most array slots the whole read may decode — every array's
  length (column, list child, struct field, dictionary — every replacement again; under `ReadOptions.columns` only the
  projected columns' and the dictionaries they use, inner ones included) summed over every batch, plus every row,
  list element and
  byte a dictionary column copies out of its dictionary. `max_rows` bounds one array; this bounds their number
  times their length, which matters where rows cost no body bytes: FixedSizeBinary(0), FixedSizeList(0) and Null
  children, and one large dictionary entry selected by many one-byte indices. The reader spends up to ~16 bytes
  per slot on offsets and selectors. `File.readBatch` / `readAll` decode within what the file's metadata left of
  the budget, each call afresh.
- `ReadOptions.max_body_bytes` (default 2^31, ours): the most bytes the compressed bodies of the WHOLE read may
  expand to — every buffer of every record and dictionary batch of the stream, or of every block of a file
  (`openFile` inflates them all). zstd reaches ~32 000:1 on a run of one byte, so a per-message cap would let K
  small messages expand K times. A declared length above what the zstd frames can hold
  (`zstd.decompressBound`), a frame that decodes to another length, or a broken frame is `error.Malformed`.
- **File footer blocks**: each `Block`'s `metaDataLength` (framing + padded metadata) and `bodyLength` must be
  those of the message at its offset, and no two blocks may share bytes (`error.Malformed`) — K blocks naming one
  message would otherwise be inflated and decoded K times. The footer's metadata version is checked like a
  message's. `File.batchRows(i)` and `File.readBatch(i)` past the last batch are `error.Unsupported`.
- **Metadata version**: V4 (Arrow 0.8–0.17) and V5 (1.0 on) are read; V1–V3 and values the format does not name
  are `error.Unsupported`. The writer writes V5.
- **UTF-8**: the writer refuses a `.text` cell (a categorical's dictionary included) that is not UTF-8
  (`error.InvalidUtf8`) — Arrow's Utf8 requires it and arrow-rs fails the whole file otherwise; the same bytes
  declared `.binary` are written as Binary. The reader checks every Utf8 / LargeUtf8 value and dictionary entry
  (`error.InvalidUtf8`) unless `ReadOptions.validate_utf8 = false`.
- **Decimal precision**: the writer declares Decimal128(p, 12) with p the digits of the column's widest value (at
  least 12, so scale ≤ precision); a value of 39 digits (an i128 can hold it, Decimal128 cannot) is
  `Unsupported`. The reader refuses a declared precision outside 1–38 (`Malformed`), and a value with more digits
  than its declared precision, or with more than 38 once at 12 fractional digits, like an inexact scale.
- **Shared dictionaries**: two fields may name one dictionary id when their value types agree (type, zone,
  children, and the children's own dictionary encodings: id, index type, order); each keeps its own index type.
  Different value types are `Malformed`; one dictionary with two `isOrdered` flags is `Unsupported`. A dictionary
  inside its own values (a cycle through the ids) is `Malformed`.
- **Dictionary batches**: a delta before the dictionary's first batch, a replacement in a file → `Malformed`.
- `dataframe` keeps list offsets in `u32`: more than 2^32 − 1 elements in one list column → `Unsupported`; the
  writer's Int32 list offsets refuse more than 2^31 − 1 elements in one batch.
- **Values `dataframe` cannot hold, or holds only inexactly** fail the whole read with `error.Unsupported` by
  default: a Decimal128 that does not fit 12 fractional digits in an i128 (or the precision rules above); a time of
  day outside `[0, 24h)`; a date outside the years 0000–9999; s/ms timestamps or durations whose microseconds
  overflow i64; a nanosecond timestamp, duration or time with digits past the microsecond; a Date64 that is not on
  a day boundary. `ReadOptions.lossy = true` reads the first four as null cells, TRUNCATES the last two toward
  zero (so −1 ns reads as 0 µs and a Date64 of −1 ms as 1970-01-01 — the day of the truncated count, not the
  calendar day of the instant), and reads a timestamp zone `tz` does not know as a naive column. Nothing else
  changes (a malformed stream is still an error). Tests: `src/stream_test.zig` "lossy: …", "inexact time
  conversions", and the `datetime` and `decimal` golden sets.
- Refused on read (`Unsupported`): LZ4_FRAME body compression, Interval, Union,
  tensors. Every structural defect — a buffer shorter than its node, offsets running backwards or past the data, an
  index outside its dictionary, node or buffer counts not matching the schema, a column length not the batch's —
  is `error.Malformed`.

## Anchoring

**External anchor (2026-11-17):** the apache/arrow-testing integration golden files written by Arrow C++,
committed under `src/testdata/` (Apache-2.0 data, see `NOTICE`; commit `5a26d357`), read by
`src/golden_test.zig`. Each set's `.stream` and `.arrow_file` is compared field by field and cell by cell with
its Arrow integration JSON (`.json.gz`), through an oracle written from the JSON's own encoding (units, decimal
scales, hex binary, dictionary indices, offsets; dates by Hinnant's `civil_from_days`), not through the reader.
Sets: `custom_metadata`, `dictionary`, `dictionary_unsigned`, `duplicate_fieldnames`, `extension`, `nested`,
`nested_large_offsets`, `null`, `null_trivial`, `primitive`, `primitive_large_offsets`, `primitive_no_batches`,
`primitive_zerolength`, `recursive_nested`, `nested_dictionary` (a list dictionary of dictionary-encoded items and a
struct dictionary whose two fields share one), from `4.0.0-shareddict` `shared_dict` (two columns, one
dictionary), and from `2.0.0-compression` `zstd` and `uncompressible_zstd`
(ZSTD body compression), from `cpp-21.0.0` `decimal32`, `decimal64`, `run_end_encoded`, `binary_view` and
`list_view`, and `map` and `map_non_canonical` (a Map as a list of its entries; the latter's `.stream`, written
by Arrow C++, carries the canonical `entries` / `key` / `value` names, its `.arrow_file` the JSON's own, and
either is accepted as the file's); `datetime`, `decimal` and (from
`cpp-21.0.0`) `decimal256` are `Unsupported` by default and compared under `lossy` (the Decimal256 oracle parses
the JSON's 77-digit values as i256).
Stream and file read equal, each file batch has its JSON batch's length, and the frame this module writes back
(plain and zstd, stream and file) reads equal, its metadata too (in the frame's shape: a run-end encoded field's
children are its values'). `interval`, `union` and `lz4` are asserted `Unsupported`, lossy
or not. No integration golden replaces a dictionary (the integration JSON cannot express one), so replacement is
anchored on the behaviour cited under "Dictionaries" and hand-built streams (`src/dict_test.zig`). The writer's bytes are anchored
only through the reader (no foreign reader runs here).

**Anchor grade:** class A · oracle EXTERNAL

## What is deliberately not done

- **Zero-copy reading — not now.** The reader copies every buffer into `dataframe` storage, which has its own
  layout (u32 list offsets, usize text offsets, 64-bit validity words); views over the input would need a second
  column representation. Revisit only with a consumer that reads files larger than memory.
- **The C data interface, Flight, compute kernels — never here.** Separate concerns (in-process FFI, RPC,
  compute) for separate modules if a consumer ever needs them.
- **LZ4_FRAME — superseded by something external:** waits for an `lz4` codec module in the collection; writing
  LZ4 is not planned even then (ZSTD is what Arrow C++ and arrow-rs recommend).
- **Reading the types `dataframe` has no column for — never as such.** Interval and Union would need new
  `dataframe` column kinds first. (RunEndEncoded, the view types and Map are read, but only as the plain columns
  they encode — Map as a list of its entries struct; writing them would need column kinds of their own.)

## Open

- The writer is anchored only through our own reader: no foreign implementation reads our bytes (a live pyarrow
  round trip needs a venv + wheel — owner decision).
- LZ4_FRAME body compression: `Unsupported` until the collection has an LZ4 codec (a new-module idea; not filed
  from this wave).
- The reader copies every buffer (no zero-copy views over the input).
- `openFile` reads the schema from the footer only; it does not compare it with the stream schema at offset 8.
- Performance not measured.
- RunEndEncoded requires `values.length == run_ends.length` per batch (Arrow C++ is believed to refuse only
  fewer values than runs). Relaxing it needs a per-batch values base in the run index, or another batch's
  values would be picked silently.
- Written key/value metadata (schema, field, footer) is read back only by this module's own reader; a future
  differential oracle should carry one metadata case, footer included.
- Compressed view batches (`prepare` splitting variadic buffers before a zstd `inflate`) have no test: the writer
  never emits views and the `cpp-21.0.0` view goldens are uncompressed.
- Message-level `custom_metadata` (on each Schema / RecordBatch / DictionaryBatch message) is neither surfaced
  nor written; only schema, field and footer metadata are.

## Plan

Oracle: the apache/arrow-testing integration golden files with their JSON descriptions (data only, Apache-2.0); a live
pyarrow round trip is an owner decision. Out: the C data interface, Flight, compute kernels.

## Backlog / deferred

From the 2026-11-17 scope survey (`## Compared with`). **Propose to implement** = substantial for a user of the
competing libraries and cheap enough to finish in one wave; none of them is started.

**Propose to implement**

- ✅ 2026-11-17 **View types and ListView on read.** Done as sketched. A message's `variadicBufferCounts` must
  have one entry per view field (pre-order) and the buffers must number the fixed ones plus their sum
  (`Malformed`); each valid row's view is checked against its batch's variadic buffers (index, offset and length
  in range, the 4-byte prefix equal to the data's start) and copied, every copied byte charged to `max_cells`
  before the copy is allocated (views may share bytes); Utf8View is UTF-8 checked; a Utf8View dictionary reads
  as a categorical. A list view's offset and size must lie within its batch's child; its selectors are checked
  against `max_cells` before allocation. Null rows' views, offsets and sizes are not looked at. Projection
  skips a view field's variadic buffers with its views. Anchored on the `cpp-21.0.0` `binary_view` and
  `list_view` goldens. Was: BinaryView / Utf8View (16-byte views, ≤ 12 bytes inline, else a buffer
  index and offset into the variadic data buffers) read into `binary` / `text`; ListView / LargeListView (offsets
  plus sizes, any order, overlap allowed) read into a `list` by copying each row's slice. Why: C++, arrow-rs and
  polars write the view encoding (polars chooses by `compat_level`), so a file from them is `Unsupported` today.
  Sketch: new `Kind`s in the reader's `plan`, bounds-checked per view against the data buffers and
  `max_cells`; the writer stays Utf8 / Binary / List. Effort: ~1 wave.
- **LZ4_FRAME bodies, read and write — after the `lz4` module** (NEW-MODULES.md). pyarrow's Feather writer
  defaults to LZ4, so this is the commonest refusal a user meets. Sketch: `Compression.lz4`, the reader dispatches
  on `BodyCompression.codec` next to zstd, with the same `max_body_bytes` charge from the frame's declared
  content size (a frame without one is `Malformed`, as arrow-rs needs it). Effort: ~0.5 wave once the codec exists.
- ✅ 2026-11-17 **Schema and field key/value metadata.** Done: `ReadOptions.metadata` (an out parameter, so
  `readStream` / `readFile` / `openFile` keep their signatures) is filled with a `Metadata` — the schema's pairs,
  a `FieldMetadata` tree parallel to the frame's columns, a file footer's pairs — copied into the read's arena;
  `WriteOptions.schema_metadata` / `field_metadata` (by position) / `footer_metadata` write them (more entries
  than columns is `Unsupported`; more `children` than a field has are dropped, the field's own metadata kept; a
  run-end encoded field's children are reported as its values' since 2026-11-17, so a read's metadata always
  fits). Anchored on the
  `custom_metadata` and `extension` goldens (every set's metadata is compared with its JSON, then written back

  Decimal128.

- ✅ 2026-11-17 **Dictionary replacement in a stream.** Done as sketched, see "Dictionaries": each batch indexes the

- ✅ 2026-11-17 **A dictionary inside another dictionary's values** (the `nested_dictionary` golden) — read; the
  inner dictionary is decoded first, the outer one's values hold its categoricals (a `list` / `struct` of

  needing a categorical inner column in `dataframe`, which it already had.

**Deferred, with the reason**

- **Union (dense and sparse)** — needs a `dataframe` column kind (`boxed` has no stable meaning on the wire); same
  for the writer. Not here until `dataframe` has one.
- **Interval (YEAR_MONTH, DAY_TIME, MONTH_DAY_NANO)** — no `dataframe` column; reading as an int or a struct would
  lose the type. Needs a column kind first.
- **Zero-copy and memory-mapped reads** — the reader copies into `dataframe`'s own layout (see "What is
  deliberately not done"); a second column representation is the prerequisite, revisit with a consumer whose files
  exceed memory. polars and pyarrow both offer it.
- **Incremental IO over `std.Io.Reader` / `std.Io.Writer`** (a batch-at-a-time reader, a `StreamWriter` that
  takes frames as they are produced) — the reader holds the whole input and the writer returns a `[]u8`; a
  streaming shape changes `Reader` (it borrows `bytes` for dictionaries and footers) and needs dictionary-delta
  bookkeeping on the writer. Own design wave; do it with a consumer that needs files larger than memory.
- **Big-endian streams (byte swap on read)** — C++, Go and nanoarrow convert; the producer is s390x-class hardware
  only and the case is refused as `Unsupported` today. Cheap but nobody on common hardware writes it.
- **Feather V1** — deprecated upstream since 25.0; not planned.
- **The C data interface, tensors / sparse tensors, Flight** — out of scope for this module (see "What this
  module is, and what it is not"); a separate module if a consumer needs the first.
- **A foreign reader over our bytes** — the writer is anchored through our own reader only (pyarrow round trip,
  owner decision, see Open).
- **Performance** — never measured; a bench against arrow-rs `arrow-ipc` and pyarrow (alternating sides, best of
  several rounds, `tools/`) is the prerequisite for any `fastest` claim and for Performance leaving `not measured`.
